_comment: The ground truth for the cross-provider matcher: 22 tracks from the
user's YouTube Music playlist, each paired with the NetEase record
that holds the same recording. A 23rd track is present but is not
catalogued on NetEase at all, so it is excluded from the denominator.
The `neteaseId` values are the ones confirmed against the metadata:
the candidate's own title, its exact duration and its album all have
to agree with the YouTube upload. Six of them differ from what the
user first wrote down; the reasons are in
`durationSeconds` is the rounded length the playlist's accessibility
label reports, which is what the app actually has. `durationExact`
is the video's own `lengthSeconds`, which the app does not fetch.
`variants` are the alternative spellings of the title that a search
has to try: a romanisation, a translation, a context annotation.

cases.youtubeAlbum: Flower Of Scotland: Timeless Classics from the Land of the Brave
cases.note: Same album and the same length as the upload; the user's first answer (414829974) is the same recording on a different compilation.

cases.youtubeAlbum: Fan of A Fan The Album (Expanded Edition)
cases.note: The user's own answer was '31526544 or 29809963, either is fine'. The matcher prefers 30512923, which is the recording on the original album — 'Fan of A Fan The Album (Deluxe Version)' — at 225.28s against the upload's own 225s. The two the user chose are a compilation (31526544, 226.52s) and the single (29809963, 226.25s), both of which sit ~1.3s further from the upload's exact length. The album name agrees with the upload's own album field, so this is the better answer and the answer is now the confirmed one.

cases.youtubeTitle: 残酷な天使のテーゼ - Zankoku na Tenshi no Thesis
cases.note: The NetEase row is titled 残酷な天使のテｰゼ (halfwidth prolonged sound mark) and carries the romanisation as its alias. NFKC folds the two; the alias is what makes the title match at all.

cases.youtubeAlbum: Why Do We Shake In The Cold?
cases.note: The album and the length both point here; the user's first answer (1479407252) is the single release of the same recording.
The title and the length both point here; the user's first answer (2041799838) is the album's title track.
Not in NetEase's catalogue at all. No algorithm can match what is not there, so this case is excluded from the denominator.

cases.youtubeTitle: We Don't Talk Anymore (feat. Selena Gomez)
cases.note: The title carries the credit, so the credit-bearing release is the right one — even though the platform ranks the plain release higher.

cases.youtubeAlbum: 家庭教師ヒットマンREBORN! オリジナル サウンドトラック ~標的2~
cases.note: The source artist is the placeholder 'Various Artists', which says nothing about who performed it and so cannot veto a match.
The studio recording; the user's first answer (2639918917) is the Acoustic version, three seconds longer.
The NetEase row is titled 'Gentleman' and carries 演奏曲 on a second release of the same recording. Without 演奏曲 in the version-word list the two are indistinguishable.

cases.youtubeTitle: 无名的人 (电影《雄狮少年》主题曲/片尾曲)
cases.note: The parenthetical is a context annotation, not part of the name. It has to be stripped before the title is compared.

The Chinese platforms file a collaboration as 'True Colors(合作音乐人:Nicki Minaj)'. Two things had to be fixed for this one: the credit marker was not recognised (so the source silently lost its credit, and the credit tier then ranked the candidate carrying '(feat. Nicki Minaj)' BELOW every same-titled cover), and the query was sent with the Chinese marker in it (so NetEase returned a page of unrelated songs and the record was not on it at all). The user confirmed the id by hand.
